scope: End-to-end reference architecture means a durable, auditable loop that connects demand/incident intake; specification and planning; isolated implementation; deterministic test/security/review; governed merge and artifact creation; progressive deployment; telemetry and SLO evaluation; rollback or repair proposal; and learning through curated eval/policy/spec updates. It excludes a mere multi-agent role diagram or an issue-to-PR tool. Evidence covers GitLab, GitHub Copilot, OpenHands, Sentry Seer, Microsoft’s starter blueprint, GitOps/Argo/OpenTelemetry/SLSA/NIST foundations, and independent benchmark/productivity evidence. [S1-S21]
current_state: Verified: no reviewed source implements and validates all seven stages as one autonomous product. The closest single SDLC surface is GitLab Duo Agent Platform: planner/developer/review/CI-repair/security flows are GA in 18.8, but production deployment, telemetry-driven repair, and governed learning remain separate integrations. [S2-S6]

Verified: Microsoft’s reference repository makes requirements-to-validated-code explicit with structured artifacts and a resolution gate, but its documented pipeline ends at code validation. [S1] GitHub Copilot cloud agent and OpenHands cover asynchronous issue/event-to-PR work in isolated or cloud execution, not self-authorized release and operation. [S7-S8]

Vendor-claimed but mechanically documented: Sentry Seer closes part of observe-to-repair by using telemetry for root-cause analysis and PR creation or handoff; Seer Agent remains open beta and has an acknowledged fine-grained-access gap. [S9]

Production-ready building blocks exist for the deterministic control plane: GitOps reconciliation, progressive delivery analysis/abort, vendor-neutral telemetry, rulesets, provenance and SSDF controls. [S10-S15,S21] The end-to-end composition and its semantics are custom engineering.

Inference: safe autonomy is feasible today for narrow, reversible, well-tested change classes. Unattended product prioritization, ambiguous feature work, production diagnosis, and automatic policy self-modification remain experimental because benchmark validity and field productivity are unsettled. [S16-S20]

representative_systems.coverage: Plan/build/review/CI repair/security within one DevSecOps control surface; custom flows and session audit. Closest integrated blueprint, but docs do not connect production telemetry to deployment or learning automatically.
representative_systems.status: Core platform and named flows GA; some REST triggers/features experimental; vendor product evidence. [S2-S6]

representative_systems.coverage: Assessor → resolver → specifier → generator → validator with file contracts and guardrails.
representative_systems.status: Reference code, created 2026; early and not a production operating system. [S1]

representative_systems.coverage: Issue, schedule or event → ephemeral worktree/environment → tests → branch/PR → human review.
representative_systems.status: Useful implementation workers, not end-to-end controllers. [S7-S8]

representative_systems.coverage: Errors/traces/logs/profiles/code → RCA/plan → PR or external-agent handoff; pre-merge AI review.
representative_systems.status: Narrow observe/repair bridge; some functions beta and claims vendor-supplied. [S9]

representative_systems.coverage: Versioned desired state; continuous reconciliation; canary/blue-green analysis; traces/metrics/logs.
representative_systems.status: Mature operational substrate; deliberately does not decide semantic repairs. [S10-S12,S15]

representative_systems.coverage: Policy enforcement, required evidence, artifact provenance and secure-development practice.

primary_evidence: GitLab documents actual trigger, runner, context and output mechanics: issues/mentions become draft MRs; code review is a CI job; failing pipelines yield suggestions/new MRs or escalation; users retain accept/modify/reject control and API calls are audited. [S3-S6]

Microsoft publishes the only source reviewed that calls itself an Agentic SDLC reference architecture, with explicit structured handoffs and ambiguity resolution. Its README’s terminal output is validator review/code, establishing the missing Ops half rather than implying it. [S1]
GitHub and OpenHands document isolated asynchronous coding and PR production. Sentry documents telemetry-to-RCA-to-PR. These form a composable seam at issue/PR/repository APIs. [S7-S9]
OpenGitOps, Argo, OpenTelemetry, SLSA, NIST SSDF, Google SRE canary practice and repository rulesets provide non-LLM invariants for deployment and assurance. [S10-S15,S21]
independent_evidence: SWE-bench established that real repository repair requires cross-file context and execution; its original best result was only 1.96%, but this is a 2023-era historical baseline, not a present product score. [S16]

SWE-rebench shows why impressive static leaderboards are not sufficient architecture evidence: fresh tasks suggest contamination can inflate some SWE-bench Verified results, and neither benchmark measures safe production deployment or incident learning. [S17]

METR’s early-2025 RCT measured a 19% slowdown for 16 experienced maintainers on their own repositories, then labeled the result outdated. Its 2026 follow-up saw raw speedup signals but declared them unreliable because selection and measurement changed. This conflict argues for local controlled trials, not universal ROI assumptions. [S18-S19]

DORA 2025’s system-level conclusion is that AI amplifies the organization already present. Though vendor-sponsored, it independently supports investment in testability, platform and feedback systems before greater autonomy. [S20]

metrics.value: GitLab’s named plan/build/review/CI repair flows reached GA in 18.8. Microsoft starter API metadata showed only 14 stars/5 forks on 2026-09-13.
metrics.caveat: GA and repository popularity measure availability/interest, not successful unattended lifecycle completion. [S1-S6]

metrics.value: SWE-bench: 2,294 issues, 12 Python repositories; Claude 2 solved 1.96% in original evaluation.
metrics.caveat: Obsolete as a current capability estimate and only patch-level. [S16]

metrics.value: SWE-rebench: >21,000 interactive Python tasks and a continuously fresh evaluation method.
metrics.caveat: Authors find possible contamination inflation for some models; no deploy/operate outcome. [S17]

metrics.value: Early-2025 METR: 19% slower. 2026 follow-up raw estimates: 18% speedup returning developers (CI -38% to +9%) and 4% new recruits (CI -15% to +9%).
metrics.caveat: Later intervals cross zero; authors judge selection and time measurement unreliable. [S18-S19]

metrics.value: No source reports a denominator-based rate for autonomous plan→production→observe→repair→learn completions, escaped defects, rollback rate, or cost per accepted durable outcome.
metrics.caveat: Unknown, not zero; product documentation is not an evaluation.

reference_workflow: 1. Intake/trigger: accept a typed event from issue tracker, dependency/security alert, CI failure, SLO burn, or user feedback. Persist immutable event ID, repository/release/trace links, business owner, severity, budget and allowed action class. Never pass raw untrusted telemetry or issue text directly to privileged tools.

2. Triage and plan: a planner retrieves only allowlisted repository, runbook and telemetry context; generates hypothesis, scope, acceptance tests, risk tier, rollout/rollback plan and missing questions. For feature work, use assessor/resolver/specifier artifacts like S1. Unknown or high-risk items transition to NEEDS_CLARIFICATION, not BUILDING. [S1,S9]

3. Policy admission: deterministic policy maps risk tier to permissions. Low-risk docs/tests/dependency patches may proceed. Auth/security/data/schema/billing/infrastructure changes require named owner approval. Create a short-lived job identity and isolated worktree/container with outbound network deny-by-default. [S8,S13-S14]

4. Build: one implementation agent edits a branch; another process records tool calls, prompt/model/version, input hashes, cost and artifacts. Run formatter, compiler, focused tests, full regression, SAST/secret/dependency/license scans, and generate provenance. A retry must start from a known commit and consume a bounded retry/cost budget. [S3,S7-S8,S13]

5. Independent review: submit a draft PR. Deterministic rulesets require checks; CODEOWNERS/human reviews high-risk code. An AI reviewer may add findings but must not be the sole approver of its own or sibling-agent output. CI-repair agents return suggestions/new PRs and escalate security-sensitive or low-context failures. [S4-S5,S21]

6. Merge/build/release: protected merge queue produces a signed, immutable artifact with SBOM/provenance. GitOps changes desired state by reviewed commit; deployment credentials are held by reconciler, never coding agent. [S10,S13]

7. Progressive deploy: dev/staging first, then a time-boxed canary. Argo analysis queries SLO/error/latency/business guardrails; PASS advances, FAIL aborts/rolls back, INCONCLUSIVE pauses for a human. [S11,S15]

8. Observe: OpenTelemetry correlates release SHA, PR, artifact digest, feature flag and agent-run ID across traces/metrics/logs. Alert deduplication creates an incident evidence bundle. Sentry-like RCA can propose a diagnosis and patch PR, but cannot suppress alerts or deploy independently. [S9,S12]

9. Repair: first choose reversible operational actions from an allowlist (rollback, disable flag, scale within cap). Code repair enters the same branch/PR/test/canary loop; never patch production directly. Repeated failure, high blast radius or budget exhaustion transitions to HUMAN_INCIDENT. [S9-S11]

10. Learn: after verified observation window, label outcome accepted/rejected/rolled-back/escaped-defect; attach reviewer edits, test gaps, time/cost and SLO delta. Add sanitized examples to a versioned local eval set. Humans review changes to prompts, policies, runbooks and acceptance tests; canary workflow-policy releases separately. DORA’s amplifier finding makes this socio-technical step essential. [S17-S20]
integration_points: Event bus/queue: GitHub/GitLab issue, PR/MR, workflow/job, security advisory and deployment webhooks; Sentry/alertmanager events. Use idempotency keys and an outbox so redelivery does not create duplicate branches or deploys. [S3-S9]

State store: relational workflow state machine plus append-only audit/artifact store. Store event→plan→commit→checks→artifact digest→deployment→telemetry→outcome links; do not treat chat history as durable state.

Agent execution: GitHub Actions ephemeral environment, GitLab runners, or self-hosted sandbox. Broker issues task-scoped tokens; repository app is restricted to selected repos; secrets are injected only to the exact CI/deploy step. [S3-S8]

Context/tool plane: allowlisted read APIs for repositories, issues, jobs, telemetry and docs; MCP only through an audited gateway with per-tool schemas, output size limits and prompt-injection filtering. GitLab lists its ai_workflows API surface and audit events. [S6]
Assurance plane: branch/ruleset APIs, CI checks, scanners, provenance/SBOM/signing and policy engine. [S13-S14,S21]
Delivery plane: artifact registry plus GitOps config repository; reconciler pulls desired state; Argo Rollouts queries metrics providers and emits promotion/abort. [S10-S11]
Observation/feedback: OTLP into Collector/backends; release markers and trace IDs feed Sentry-like RCA; curated outcomes feed offline evals, never live weight/policy updates. [S9,S12,S17]
human_gates: Clarify business intent, priority, nonfunctional requirements and ambiguous acceptance criteria before specification; the Microsoft resolver gate can be automated only when source documents contain explicit answers. [S1]
Approve elevated tool scope or any external network/secret access. Separate requester, agent service identity and approver.

Require human/code-owner approval for public APIs, auth/crypto, user data, schema/destructive migration, billing, infrastructure/permissions, incident severity 1-2, policy/prompt changes and agent-generated tests that define acceptance. [S14,S21]

Require a human at INCONCLUSIVE canary, conflicting telemetry, unknown root cause, repeated CI/repair failure, material cost overrun, or rollback failure. Argo explicitly supports inconclusive analysis; GitLab CI repair explicitly escalates low-context/security-sensitive cases. [S5,S11]

Permit auto-merge/deploy only for pre-approved low-risk classes with all independent checks, small blast radius, reversible state and proven local historical precision. Periodically sample even successful automated changes.
failure_modes: Specification failure: plausible code satisfies an underspecified prompt but not user need; evaluator/tests generated from the same flawed assumption create correlated false confidence. [S1]

Context/tool failure: stale index, missing cross-repo contract, oversized logs, transient runner, hallucinated API, model drift, nondeterministic retry, or broad app permissions. OpenHands’ documented repository/Actions/workflow access illustrates the blast radius. [S8]

Security: prompt injection in issue/log/dependency text, secret exfiltration, poisoned tool/MCP response, malicious dependency, artifact substitution, privilege escalation, and an agent approving its own work. [S13-S14]
Quality/evaluation: tests pass but are weak; benchmark contamination inflates expectations; issue-to-patch success does not predict production correctness. [S16-S17]

Delivery: nonreproducible artifact, configuration drift, schema incompatibility, canary metric blindness, delayed failure, noisy metric, false rollback or rollback that cannot undo data mutation. [S10-S15]
Repair oscillation: monitor triggers agent, patch creates new symptom, repeated agents issue conflicting changes, or alert suppression hides harm. Use one incident lease and cooldown.
Learning corruption: successful short observation window labels a latent regression positive; raw customer data enters eval/prompts; an agent self-modifies policy to optimize proxy metrics.

Organization/economics: review queues become bottleneck, alert/PR spam destroys trust, token/runner cost exceeds saved labor, and maintainers spend longer correcting agents. Independent productivity estimates conflict and later measurement is biased. [S18-S20]
controls_and_mitigations: Capability security: deny-by-default network, sandbox, read-only context phase, separate write token, task/repo/path/tool allowlists, short TTL, no production credential in coding runtime, concurrency/rate/cost ceilings, and immediate kill switch. [S8,S13-S14]

Change security: protected branches/rulesets, mandatory status checks and code owners; signed commits/artifacts, SBOM, SLSA provenance verification; two-person control for policy, identity and deployment changes. [S13-S14,S21]

Evidence diversity: keep planner, implementer, test oracle and reviewer independent where possible; require deterministic compilation/tests/scans; mutation/property/contract tests for critical paths; never accept model confidence as a check.

Release safety: GitOps pull reconciliation, staged environments, feature flags, canary comparison, minimum sample/window, abort on guardrail violation, pause on inconclusive, tested rollback and backup/restore. [S10-S11,S15]

Operational containment: deduplicate by incident/release fingerprint, one active repair lease, capped retries, exponential backoff, repair cooldown, maximum blast radius, rollback-first playbooks, and human escalation.

Audit/privacy: immutable lineage of prompts/tool calls/model/config/artifacts/approvals; redact telemetry and customer data before LLM context; retention/deletion policy; replay eval before model/prompt upgrades. GitLab API audit and Sentry’s acknowledged org-wide access caveat show both a mechanism and a gap. [S6,S9]

Learning safety: version eval sets/policies; prevent online self-edit; human-review proposed learning; shadow and canary new workflow versions; track escaped defect, rollback, reviewer-edit, false-alert and cost rates by change class. [S17-S20]
maturity_assessment: Conditionally useful, not autonomously end-to-end production-ready. Plan/build/PR/test, deterministic CI/CD, GitOps, telemetry and rollback are separately production-grade. Narrow CI and telemetry-to-PR repair is commercially available. A single governed loop across product planning, code, deployment, operations and learning is emerging: GitLab is closest in SDLC breadth but lacks a documented production-telemetry/learning closure; Sentry supplies a narrow Ops bridge; Microsoft supplies an early Dev reference. Independent evidence tests patches or human task time rather than full-loop safety, and contamination/selection disputes remain. Grade: production-ready for deterministic substrate and low-risk supervised proposals; conditionally useful for auto-merge/canary of allowlisted changes; experimental for automatic incident code repair; speculative for self-changing policy or unattended product direction. [S1-S21]
build_vs_buy: Buy/integrate the commodity control plane: GitHub or GitLab repository/issue/CI/rulesets; hosted coding agent or OpenHands; Sentry or another telemetry/RCA layer; OpenTelemetry; artifact signing/provenance; GitOps and Argo-style progressive delivery. GitLab reduces seams for plan-to-CI repair; GitHub/OpenHands allow more modular workers; Sentry is the clearest documented observe-to-PR bridge. Build the organization-specific orchestration: typed event/state model, risk classifier, scoped credential broker, context gateway, acceptance-test policy, cross-tool lineage, SLO/canary rules, repair lease/deduplication, outcome labeling, local eval harness and human escalation UI. Do not buy a role-playing multi-agent framework and mistake it for lifecycle assurance. [S1-S15,S21]
recommended_pattern: Adopt a hub-and-spoke, proposal-first architecture. The hub is a deterministic workflow engine/policy engine with durable state and append-only evidence. Replaceable agent workers may plan, code, review or diagnose, but they have no standing production authority. Repository PR/MR is the universal change contract; signed artifact digest and GitOps commit are the release contracts; OpenTelemetry release-linked evidence is the operations contract. Start at Level 0 observe-only; Level 1 agent drafts PRs; Level 2 auto-merge only docs/tests/low-risk dependency patches after measured precision; Level 3 auto-canary reversible application changes with SLO abort; keep migrations, identity, money, sensitive data and workflow-policy changes human-gated. Promote each change class only after a local trial reports acceptance, reviewer-edit, escaped-defect, rollback, MTTR, cost and false-action rates. This architecture preserves tool portability, limits correlated agent error and turns learning into reviewed configuration/evals rather than uncontrolled self-modification. [S3-S15,S17-S21]
open_questions: What is the full-loop completion denominator and rate by change class, including rejected plans, abandoned PRs, canary aborts and latent regressions? No reviewed source reports it.
Can an independent oracle detect semantic/product mistakes when planner, code and tests share model/data lineage?

How should provenance cover prompts, retrieved context, tool versions and model snapshots without leaking secrets or personal data? SLSA covers source/build artifacts, not the full agent reasoning supply chain. [S13]
What observation window and counterfactual establish that a repair caused improvement rather than coinciding with traffic change?
How portable are GitLab custom flows and Sentry handoffs across self-managed installations, multi-repo systems and regulated data boundaries? [S2,S6,S9]
Which workflow-level benchmark measures deploy safety, incident precision, rollback and learning quality on fresh tasks? SWE-rebench fixes some patch contamination but not this scope. [S17]
What are reliable current productivity and total-cost effects under concurrent agents? METR says its newer design is biased and time accounting breaks under concurrency. [S19]

confidence.overall: Moderate-high for documented mechanics and the conclusion that components exist but no validated unified autonomous loop was found; moderate for comparative maturity; low for market-wide absence and ROI.

claim_level.high: GitLab/GitHub/OpenHands/Sentry documented triggers, permissions, outputs and release-control standards; benchmark sample/result statements. [S1-S19,S21]
claim_level.moderate: GitLab is the closest reviewed integrated SDLC surface; compositional architecture and maturity categories. Broad search was constrained, and vendor docs can omit failures.
claim_level.low: Production prevalence, unattended success rate and total economics because no audited full-loop case study or denominator-based metric was found; 2026 METR evidence is explicitly unreliable. [S19]

conflicts: Availability versus efficacy: GitLab marks platform/flows GA, while GA only indicates supported availability; no independent full-loop reliability result accompanies it. [S2-S6]

Benchmark optimism versus freshness: current agent marketing/leaderboards imply strong repair capability, but SWE-rebench reports contamination may inflate some SWE-bench Verified performance. Both are patch benchmarks, not deployment evidence. [S16-S17]

Productivity direction changed: METR measured 19% slowdown in early 2025 and later raw speedup estimates; METR itself labels the first outdated and the second unreliable due to selection, pay and concurrency measurement. Likely explanation is improving tools plus non-comparable samples/tasks. [S18-S19]

Autonomy versus control: vendors describe agents as autonomous, but actual safe mechanics terminate in staged changes, suggestions or PRs controlled by users/rulesets. This is useful bounded agency, not autonomous lifecycle ownership. [S1-S9,S21]

Continuous reconciliation versus semantic repair: GitOps automatically corrects runtime state to declared desired state; it cannot infer a correct new desired state or code patch. Treating reconciliation as self-healing software conflates two different capabilities. [S10]

uncertain.claim: No production deployment has ever connected every stage in one implementation.
uncertain.reason: Absence cannot be proven; reviewed primary sources and independent studies yielded no auditable end-to-end case with denominators. Private internal systems may exist.
uncertain.impact: Do not phrase as universal nonexistence; say no validated reviewed example was found.

uncertain.reason: Repository was created in 2026 and had small public activity indicators; stars/forks are not usage or outcome measures.
Early METR RCT is outdated; 2026 follow-up has confidence intervals crossing zero and serious selection/concurrency bias.
uncertain.impact: Require local randomized or phased measurement. [S18-S19]

uncertain.claim: Sentry Seer RCA/fix precision and safe auto-trigger performance.
uncertain.reason: Mechanics and limitations are documented, but no independent precision, accepted-PR, regression or MTTR denominator was found.
uncertain.impact: Use advisory/PR mode and measure locally. [S9]

uncertain.claim: Future version/status drift after the as-of date.
uncertain.reason: Living vendor documentation changes; exact behavior depends on tier, flags, model and hosted/self-managed version.
uncertain.impact: Pin product/model/workflow versions and revalidate before implementation. [S2-S9]

uncertain.reason: Configured Serper web search was unavailable. Research used direct official URLs, repository API/document traversal and known academic sources; Chinese/community discovery was therefore less broad than planned.
uncertain.impact: Moderate confidence in the landscape, lower confidence in universal absence and regional alternatives.
